title: Kosovo Joins the Team! Another Country Signs Up for Gaza Peacekeeping Force
summary:
Have you ever been part of a big team project? Well, countries are teaming up to help bring peace to Gaza, a place that has been through a terrible war. The latest country to join is Kosovo, a small nation in Europe.

On Monday, Kosovo signed a formal agreement to join the International Stabilization Force (ISF). That's a group of soldiers from different countries who will go to Gaza to help keep things calm. The agreement was signed by Kosovo's Security Force Commander and the US commander of the force.

Kosovo is not the only country joining. Indonesia, Morocco, Kazakhstan, Albania, and Uganda have also agreed to send troops. But Turkey won't be there because Israel said no.

The ISF is part of a bigger peace plan that was made one year ago. The plan has 20 points, and one of them is to create this multinational force. The soldiers will help train a Palestinian police force and make sure weapons are put away.

But there are some problems. Israel and the other countries can't agree on when Israeli soldiers will leave Gaza and when Hamas (a group that fights Israel) will give up its weapons. A leader of the peace effort, Nikolay Mladenov, said they are still working on making sure everyone does what they promised.

The United States is putting more than $206 million into this force. That money will pay for equipment, vehicles, and other things the soldiers need.

So, Kosovo is now part of a big international team. It's like adding another player to the squad. Will they be able to help bring peace to Gaza? Everyone is watching to see.
why_it_matters: Wars don't end just because fighting stops — countries still have to work together to make peace hold, and this story shows how joining a team can help rebuild a place.

background_read: Gaza (a small piece of land along the Mediterranean Sea where many Palestinians live) has been through a terrible war, and many countries are trying to help it become calm.
Kosovo (a small country in Europe) was once at war, so its people understand how important peace can be.
When countries join together to send soldiers after a conflict, it is called an international force, and the soldiers are meant to protect peace and help rebuild trust.
Article_Structure: WHO: Kosovo's Security Force Commander signed the agreement with the U.S. commander of the force, on behalf of Kosovo.
WHAT: Kosovo became the newest country to join the International Stabilization Force for Gaza.
WHERE: Kosovo is the country joining, Gaza is where the force will go, and Israel is part of the negotiations.
WHY: The force will help train a Palestinian police force and make sure weapons are put away after the war.

perspectives.description: They see helping in Gaza as part of a big international team effort, and every new country adds soldiers and support.
If the force works, it could mean fewer weapons, safer streets, and a real step toward peace after a destructive war.
There are still big disagreements about when Israeli soldiers will leave and when Hamas will give up its weapons, so success is not guaranteed.
